<problem>
For a nonempty finite poset $S$, a linear extension is a total order on its underlying set that extends its partial order. Its order dimension $\dim S$ is the least positive integer $t$ for which there are linear extensions $L_1,\ldots,L_t$ such that $x\le_S y$ if and only if $x\le_{L_i}y$ for every $i$.

For each positive integer $k$, write $[k]=\{1,\ldots,k\}$. Let $\lambda(k)$ be the number of inclusion-maximal intersecting families of subsets of $[k]$: a family $\mathcal F$ is intersecting when $A\cap B\ne\varnothing$ for all $A,B\in\mathcal F$, including $A=B$, and it is inclusion-maximal when no proper larger family of subsets of $[k]$ is intersecting.

Fix an integer $d\ge8$ and put $M_d=\lambda(d-1)+1$. Let $Q_d$ be the poset consisting of all one-element and two-element subsets of $[M_d]$, ordered by inclusion. For a nonempty finite poset $P$, order $P\times Q_d$ by $(p,A)\le(p',A')$ exactly when $p\le_P p'$ and $A\subseteq A'$.

Let $F(d)$ be the supremum of $\dim(P\times Q_d)-\dim P$ as $P$ ranges over all nonempty finite posets with $\dim P\ge3$. Determine $F(d)$ exactly for every integer $d\ge8$.
</problem>

548	## 6. Completing both halves
549	
550	### Upper bound
551	
552	Let \(\dim P=r\ge3\). For some \(m\), a realizer embeds \(P\) into \(C_m^r\). By (3),
553	\[
554	P\times Q_d
555	\hookrightarrow
556	C_m^{r-3}\times(C_m^3\times Q_d)
557	\hookrightarrow
558	\mathbb R^{r+d-3}.
559	\]
560	Hence
561	\[
562	\dim(P\times Q_d)-\dim P\le d-3. \tag{14}
563	\]
564	
565	### Matching lower bound
566	
567	We first prove \(\dim Q_d\ge d\).
568	
569	If \(d-1\) extensions realized \(Q_d\), restrict them to the singleton elements. For each vertex \(i\), let
570	\[
571	W_i(j)=\{c:i\text{ follows }j\text{ in extension }c\}.
572	\]
573	For fixed \(i\), these sets are pairwise intersecting: reversing
574	\(\{i\},\{j,k\}\) requires putting \(i\) after both \(j,k\).
575	
576	Extend them to a maximal intersecting family \(\mathcal F_i\) on \([d-1]\). For \(i\ne j\), the complementary sets \(W_i(j)\) and \(W_j(i)\) belong to \(\mathcal F_i,\mathcal F_j\), respectively. Therefore \(\mathcal F_i\ne\mathcal F_j\). This would give
577	\[
578	M_d\le\lambda(d-1),
579	\]
580	a contradiction.

582	Thus \(\dim Q_d\ge d\); (3) gives the reverse inequality.
583	
584	Now take any three-dimensional poset \(P\), for example the Boolean lattice on three elements. Its product with \(Q_d\) contains \(Q_d\), so
585	\[
586	\dim(P\times Q_d)-\dim P\ge d-3.
587	\]
588	Together with (14), this proves the answer.
